standard_prerequisites.name: Composition classes and the symmetry criterion
standard_prerequisites.statement: A is symmetric iff |A_Dbar(alpha)| depends only on the equivalence class of the composition alpha under the relation that ignores the order of parts.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion applied at source line 549 after the class sizes have been computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sparse sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: A subset of [N-1] is sparse if it contains no two consecutive integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: Sparsity of both D and J is used to run the two cases at source lines 541-547.

core_obligations: Replace the goal by symmetry for the complementary statistic Dbar, by the retained folklore lemma (source line 539).

Case max_i alpha_i > 2: find j in [N-2] with neither j nor j+1 in S_alpha, use that respect for the composition forces Dbar(a) contained in S_alpha, so D(a) contains two consecutive integers and is not sparse, whence A_Dbar(alpha) is empty (source lines 541-543).

Case max_i alpha_i <= 2: let k be the number of parts equal to 2, note that J = [N-1] minus S_alpha is sparse with exactly k elements, and show that a lies in A_Dbar(alpha) exactly when D(a) contains J (source lines 545-547).
Conclude |A_Dbar(alpha)| = b_k depends only on k, hence only on the composition class, and apply the symmetry criterion (source lines 547-549).

proof_roadmap.step: Kill composition classes with a part larger than 2 using sparsity.
Identify the class sizes with the hypothesis counts b_k.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:sufficent condition symmetry two rows` at source lines 533-537: if a finite set A with a sparse statistic D satisfies |A(D contains J)| = b_{|J|} for every sparse J, then A is symmetric for D. The author's proof (source lines 538-550) converts the hypothesis into symmetry by an indirect route: it first passes to the complementary statistic (line 539), then splits the composition classes into those with a part larger than 2, which are emptied by a two-consecutive-integers argument exploiting both sparsity of D and the definition of respecting a composition (lines 541-543), and those with all parts at most 2, where the complement of the class support is a sparse set with exactly k elements and the hypothesis literally gives the class size b_k (lines 545-547). The final step identifies the sizes as a function of the class alone and invokes the symmetry criterion. The statement mentions only the hypothesis and the conclusion, not the complement or the two-case split.
